title: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Baltimore Police Department)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I am hereby requesting access to the records listed below and held by the Baltimore Police Department.

1)	Any policies, procedures, protocols, and/or written guidance for the use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) by Baltimore Police Department. This request includes, but is not limited to policies setting forth permitted and prohibited uses for ALPRs and rules regarding who may and may not use this technology.

2)	Information about which people and agencies have access to images, videos, and raw data sets generated by ALPR systems monitored or maintained by Baltimore Police Department, under what circumstances these individuals have access to the above-mentioned data, and what information must be entered about any data requests. The list of agencies includes, but is not limited to, parking and traffic enforcement agencies, and other law enforcement agencies.

3)	Policies, procedures and information regarding Baltimore Police Department data retention and data purging practices for ALPR systems, including  Baltimore Police Department policies regarding handling images, videos, and raw data sets.

4)	Information about Baltimore Police Department audits or other procedures used to assure compliance with the above requirements.

5)	Information regarding the training that Baltimore Police Department personnel must undergo to use ALPRs, if any.

6)	ALPR training materials provided to Baltimore Police Department.

7)	Product and user manuals for all ALPR software and hardware possessed or used by Baltimore Police Department.

8)	The name of all ALPR vendors, ALPR software systems, and ALPR hardware currently used by Baltimore Police Department or by third party who make the information available to Baltimore Police Department. Hardware includes fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile devices. Software systems include optical character recognition and artificial intelligence capabilities.

9)	Description of how targets (aka “hot lists”) are shared with ALPR systems and monitored, including the sources for these data feeds.

10)	A list and map of locations where fixed-location ALPRs are currently located within Baltimore Police Department’s jurisdiction.

11)	The number of ALPR devices operated by the agency for the following categories: fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile ALPRs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, please disclose total charges in advance of fulfilling the request. Alternatively, please consider waiving any fees, pursuant to § 4-206(e)(2)(ii) of the General Provisions Article, as this request is on behalf of individuals served by the Maryland Office of the Public Defender, a state government agency, which solely serves indigent citizens of Maryland. As a result, my request for the above-listed public records is in the public interest. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available, or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff Gilleran
Chief Attorney
Forensics Division
Office of the Public Defender

Baltimore, MD 21202

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Resubmission of an unanswered request. I submitted the request below by email to sheriffs_recordsrequest@smcgov.org on September 13, 2026; a copy of that email is attached. I have received no acknowledgment, no determination, and no notice of extension, and the 10-day period for a determination under Gov. Code § 7922.535 has passed. I am resubmitting the request through this address so that the request and all correspondence about it are kept in one place. Please process it as the same request, as of its original submission date, and not as a new request with a new response period. Please send the overdue determination, and all further correspondence, to this address. The text below is unchanged from the original. Where it says "the date of this request," that means September 13, 2026.

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code § 7920.000 et seq.), I request the following records from the San Mateo County Sheriff's Office.

This request seeks existing records only (Gov. Code § 7922.530; Sierra Club v. Superior Court (2013) 57 Cal.4th 157). Each item is limited to records created on or before the date of this request.

Scope basis. The Sheriff's Office's Memorandum of Understanding with the Northern California Regional Intelligence Center ("NCRIC"), produced by the San Mateo Police Department under Public Records Act request W012376-032026, is executed by Greg Munks, Sheriff of San Mateo County, on behalf of NCRIC. To the extent the Sheriff's Office holds, creates, or retains records in an administrative or fiscal capacity for NCRIC, those records are writings "prepared, owned, used, or retained" by the Sheriff's Office within the meaning of Gov. Code § 7920.530, regardless of whether NCRIC's day-to-day IT operations are performed by NCRIC staff, a vendor, or another member agency's personnel on NCRIC's behalf. If the Sheriff's Office takes the position that it does not hold the records described below and that some other entity is the proper respondent, please identify that entity and the basis for that position in the written determination.

As you are aware, NCRIC provided ALPR data aggregation and search services to its member agencies through a platform known as "AstroMetrics," built and operated on NCRIC's behalf by MaiVERIC, Inc. MaiVERIC's November 17, 2022 press release announcing the platform's deployment quotes Brian Rodrigues, NCRIC's Assistant Deputy Director for Information Technology & Cyber Security, and states that AstroMetrics was being provided "to 70 public safety agencies" and that it "maintains all usage records" and that "[c]lient administrators also have access to real-time data ingestion and usage logs."

As you are further aware, the vendor's own published technical documentation for the AstroMetrics platform states that NCRIC used a third-party identity provider, SecureAuth, configured to authenticate users against NCRIC's own internal Active Directory, and that users were federated into the AstroMetrics application through that mechanism — an identity realm the documentation identifies as "SecureAuth5" — rather than through any login screen operated by the vendor. That same documentation reflects that non-NCRIC personnel, including accounts associated with federal agency domains, accessed the platform through this mechanism during at least the period June through December 2023.

Civil Code § 1798.90.52 provides that an ALPR operator that accesses, or provides access to, ALPR information shall maintain a record of that access including the date and time of access, the data elements used to query the system, the username of the person accessing the information, and, as applicable, the organization or entity with which that person is affiliated, and the purpose for accessing the information. As the entity that operated AstroMetrics and provided its member agencies' and other users' access to ALPR information through that platform, NCRIC is an ALPR operator within the meaning of that section as to the records described below.

Records requested, from January 1, 2021 through the date of this request:

1. Records reflecting the population of user accounts provisioned for the AstroMetrics platform (or its predecessor or successor NCRIC ALPR aggregation platform, by whatever name), by agency or organizational affiliation — including any roster, directory export, account listing, or periodic user-count report, at any point during the period covered by this request.

2. Records describing or reflecting the process by which a person or account not affiliated with an NCRIC member agency — including any person or account affiliated with a federal agency or department — was granted an AstroMetrics account, added to NCRIC's Active Directory, or federated into AstroMetrics access through the SecureAuth identity provider or any successor identity provider.

3. Any agreement, memorandum, authorization, policy, or correspondence permitting or addressing access by any federal agency or department, or by any of its personnel or contractors, to ALPR information contributed by NCRIC member agencies, whether through AstroMetrics or any other NCRIC-operated or NCRIC-affiliated system.

4. SecureAuth or Active Directory logs, reports, or exports reflecting user account creation, modification, or deletion events, and user authentication (login) events, for the identity realm bound to the AstroMetrics application (identified in the vendor's documentation as "SecureAuth5"), for the full period such logs exist.

5. Records reflecting NCRIC's or the Sheriff's Office's access to, or possession of, the access records described in Item 1 of the request captioned "NCRIC platform access data and its disposition" submitted to the San Mateo Police Department, to the extent responsive records exist independent of anything SMPD may produce.

If no records are located for any individual item, please respond to that item separately and continue processing the remaining items.

If any portion of this request is denied, please identify the specific record withheld, state the specific statutory exemption relied upon, and produce all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions (Gov. Code §§ 7922.000, 7922.525). If any item is denied on the ground that the Sheriff's Office does not hold the responsive records in its NCRIC-administrative capacity, please identify the entity that does and the basis for that position.

Please provide the determination required by Government Code § 7922.535 within 10 days, in writing, per § 7922.540. Please acknowledge receipt of this request so the record reflects the date received.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.
